title: Shafarevich-Tate groups of holomorphic Lagrangian fibrations II

predicted_errors.error_location: Proposition 4.0.1 (Section 4, also restated in Lemma 4.3.6 and Proposition 4.8.3)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Proposition 4.0.1 states: 'Suppose that the set U ⊂ 𝔻 parametrizing Kähler Shafarevich–Tate deformations of X is non-empty and 0 ∈ U. Then X is hyperkähler.' Since X = X_0 and U is defined as the set of t for which X_t is Kähler, the hypothesis '0 ∈ U' already asserts that X itself is Kähler, making the stated conclusion ('X is hyperkähler') a tautology. This contradicts the actual proof strategy (Lemma 4.3.6, Steps 1–6), which explicitly treats X_0 as possibly non-Kähler and constructs an auxiliary hyperkähler family Y to which X_0 is shown to be bimeromorphic — work that would be unnecessary if X_0 were already known to be Kähler by hypothesis. The same inconsistency recurs in Lemma 4.3.6 ('Assume that 0 ∈ U, where U ⊂ 𝔻 is the set of Kähler Shafarevich–Tate twists') and Proposition 4.8.3. The hypothesis should state that 0 lies in the closure of U (i.e., is a limit of Kähler points), not that 0 ∈ U itself.

The text states 'The period map is a biholomorphism in a neighborhood of Y_0 in M_Λ (Theorem B(2)).' However, Theorem B (stated in 1.2.2 and proven in 5.2.9) concerns H^0(X^φ,Ω²_{X^φ})=ℂσ and H^1(X^φ,ℚ)=0, and has no numbered sub-parts about the period map being a local biholomorphism. The intended citation is clearly the Local Torelli Theorem, i.e., Theorem 4.3.4(2), not 'Theorem B(2)'.

Theorem 2.1.6 is attributed to '[Voi92, Mat99]', but the bibliography contains no entry for 'Voi92' (presumably a Voisin 1992 paper). This reference is missing from the reference list, making the citation unverifiable/incomplete.

predicted_errors.error_location: Proof of Theorem A(2) (Section 3.0.6) and Proposition 5.3.9, citation [SY22]
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text cites '[SY22, Theorem 0.2]' ('The cohomology groups H^i(B, ℚ) are the same as for ℙ^n [SY22, Theorem 0.2]') and again '[SY22]' in Proposition 5.3.9's proof, but no bibliography entry for 'SY22' exists in the reference list.

The proof states 'By [Rei70] (see also [Kur]) Γ_t is a complex analytic subvariety...' but there is no 'Rei70' entry in the bibliography (only 'Ray70', a different, unrelated work by Raynaud on Picard functor specialization). The reference appears to be fabricated or missing.

The proof states 'Let h ∈ H²(X,ℝ) be the pullback of a Kähler form on Y' where the rational map is f: X^φ ⇢ Y. Since f is defined on X^φ, not X, the pullback class should live in H²(X^φ,ℝ), not H²(X,ℝ). As written, the class h is asserted to be in the wrong cohomology group for the rest of the argument (which discusses the restriction of h to fibers of π^φ) to make sense.

The remark defines the Bogomolov–Guan manifold as BG^n(S) throughout ('Consider its associated Bogomolov–Guan manifold BG^n(S)...It admits a Lagrangian fibration π': BG^n(S)→ℙ^n...'), but then states 'Theorem C also shows that the rank of the restriction map H^2(BG^n(A)) → H^2(F^n) is zero,' using 'BG^n(A)' instead of 'BG^n(S)'. A is the abelian surface used for the Kummer variety K^n(A), a different object from S (the Kodaira surface), so this is an inconsistent substitution of notation.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.8.4 (Proof of Theorem A and Proposition 4.0.1)
